title: Ambiorix's revolt
description: The Eburones under Ambiorix destroy a Roman force of about fifteen cohorts wintering in their territory, the heaviest Roman loss of Caesar's Gallic War.

title: Murder of Charles the Good
description: Count Charles of Flanders is killed at prayer, and in the succession struggle that follows the Flemish towns first act as a political force.

title: Battle of the Golden Spurs
description: Flemish town militias on foot defeat the mounted knights of the king of France, an event later made the emblem of Flemish identity.

title: Joyous Entry of Brabant
description: Duchess Joanna and Duke Wenceslaus swear a charter limiting their power over war, coinage and taxes, which later dukes had to confirm on their accession.

title: University of Leuven founded
description: A papal bull founds the first university of the Low Countries, which becomes one of the main centres of learning in northern Europe.

title: Ghent Altarpiece installed
description: The altarpiece begun by Hubert van Eyck and finished by Jan van Eyck is installed, a founding work of early Netherlandish oil painting.

title: Great Privilege
description: After the death of Charles the Bold, Mary of Burgundy grants the States General a charter restoring provincial rights that her predecessors had removed.

title: Birth of Charles V
description: The future emperor Charles V is born in Ghent, and under him the Low Countries become part of a monarchy that also holds Spain and its overseas territories.

title: Iconoclastic Fury in Antwerp
description: Crowds strip the images from the churches of Antwerp as a wave of Calvinist image-breaking crosses the Low Countries, leading Philip II to send the Duke of Alba.

title: Execution of Egmont and Horn
description: The counts of Egmont and Horn are beheaded on the orders of Alba's Council of Troubles, which hardens opposition to Spanish rule.

title: Sack of Antwerp
description: Unpaid Spanish troops plunder the city and kill thousands of its inhabitants, pushing the provinces to unite against them in the Pacification of Ghent days later.

title: Fall of Antwerp
description: After a siege of more than a year the city surrenders to the Duke of Parma, fixing the division between a Spanish south and a Dutch north and sending many of its Protestants to Holland.

title: Bombardment of Brussels
description: French artillery under Marshal Villeroi destroys the Grand-Place and about a third of the buildings of the city, which is afterwards rebuilt in its present form.

title: Battle of Fontenoy
description: A French army under Marshal Saxe defeats the British, Dutch and Austrian allies, after which France occupies most of the Austrian Netherlands until 1748.

title: United Belgian States proclaimed
description: After the Brabant Revolution drives out the Austrian army, the provinces form a confederation that lasts until Austrian troops return in December.

title: Battle of Fleurus
description: The French revolutionary army defeats the Austrians and their allies, ending Austrian rule and leading to the annexation of the Belgian provinces by France in 1795.

title: Leopold I takes the oath as king
description: Leopold of Saxe-Coburg swears allegiance to the constitution as first King of the Belgians, the day now kept as the national holiday.

title: First railway on the European continent
description: A steam railway opens between Brussels and Mechelen, the first public steam passenger line on the continent and the start of a state-planned network.

title: Treaty of London
description: The Netherlands and the great powers recognise Belgium as an independent and perpetually neutral state, the guarantee invoked when Germany invaded in 1914.

title: General strike for the vote
description: A general strike called by the Belgian Labour Party leads parliament to give every adult man a vote, with extra votes for the propertied and educated.

title: Belgium annexes the Congo
description: After international protest at the abuses of the Congo Free State, the Belgian state takes over the territory from King Leopold II as the Belgian Congo.

title: German invasion of 1914
description: German troops cross the border after Belgium refuses them passage, which brings Britain into the war and begins four years of occupation.

title: First large gas attack at Ypres
description: The German army releases chlorine gas against French and Algerian troops in the Ypres Salient, the first large-scale use of lethal gas on the Western Front.

title: German invasion of 1940
description: German forces attack on 10 May, taking the fort of Eben-Emael by glider assault, and the Belgian army surrenders eighteen days later.

title: Battle of the Bulge begins
description: The last large German offensive in the west strikes American lines in the Ardennes and is stopped within weeks, with Bastogne held under siege.

title: Referendum on the return of Leopold III
description: A majority votes for the return of the king, but the divide between Flanders and Wallonia and the strikes that follow lead him to abdicate in favour of his son Baudouin in 1951.

title: Expo 58 opens
description: The first world's fair after the Second World War opens with the Atomium as its centrepiece, in the year the European Economic Community begins work in Brussels.

title: Leuven university crisis
description: Flemish student protests demanding that the French-speaking section leave Leuven bring down the government and lead to the division of the university on language lines.

title: Belgium becomes a federal state
description: The fourth state reform rewrites the constitution to declare Belgium a federal state made up of communities and regions with their own elected parliaments.

title: Brussels bombings
description: Suicide bombers of the Islamic State group kill 32 people at Brussels Airport and Maalbeek metro station, the deadliest attack in the country's history.
